-export function build(g) {}
+// Part: lighting. Lanterns for the lobbies, flats, lofts, aisles and rear doors (plan.md "Lit interiors"; elements.md
+// last item). Hanging lanterns hang from the floor above (flats); standing ones sit on a floor or a yard block (lobby,
+// loft, aisle, rear door). Writes go into air only: a lamp with no support, or a cell an earlier part owns, is skipped.
+import { HOUSES } from "../vocab.mjs";
+/** One lantern on (x, y, z): hanging under a solid block above, or standing on a solid block below. */
+function lamp(g, x, y, z, hanging) {
+  const [sx, sy, sz] = hanging ? [x, y + 1, z] : [x, y - 1, z];
+  if (!g.isAir(x, y, z) || g.isAir(sx, sy, sz)) return false;
+  g.set(x, y, z, "lantern", { hanging: String(hanging), waterlogged: "false" });
+  return true;
+export function build(g) {
+  for (const h of Object.values(HOUSES)) {
+    const { a, lobby: [l0, l1] } = h;
+    const doorX = l1 - 1;                                    // the rear door: lobby x (H1 35, H2 23, H3 3)
+    // lobby: standing lamps on the shop floor, against the party wall side, clear of the z 7 door and z 24 door
+    lamp(g, l0, 2, 9, false);
+    lamp(g, l0, 2, 20, false);
+    // flats: hung from the floor above (flat 1 under y 13, flat 2 under y 18), two rows of lamps across the plan
+    for (const z of [11, 18]) {
+      for (const x of [a + 4, a + 9]) {
+        lamp(g, x, 12, z, true);                              // flat 1
+        lamp(g, x, 17, z, true);                              // flat 2
+    // loft: standing lamps on the loft floor (y 18), under the roof
+    for (const z of [11, 18]) for (const x of [a + 4, a + 9]) lamp(g, x, 19, z, false);
+    // service aisle behind the back walls (keeper's route, customers never enter)
+    lamp(g, a + 4, 2, 23, false);
+    // rear yard: a lamp beside each rear door, standing on the yard grass
+    lamp(g, doorX - 1, 2, 26, false);

input.summary:
parts/lights.mjs places 53 lanterns: standing lamps in each lobby (2), the service aisle and each rear door's yard; hung lamps under flat 1 and flat 2 ceilings and standing lamps in the lofts.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the lighting line reports 53 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check shows no lantern floating or unsupported.
Every lobby floor cell is at 8+; flats and lofts are dim-to-lit with 1–2 dark cells left per flat 2, measured on the empty shell before the room parts furnish it.
left: Flat 2 still has dark floor cells on the empty shell: 1 each in H1 and H2 and 2 in H3, at the rear corners and the H3 inner strip. Re-run `node $MCD light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` after the room parts (furniture and partitions change the light) and add a lamp where a cell stays at 0.
Flat 1 cells sit at 4–5 (dim, not dark) on the shell: the stub rooms have not been built, so this is mostly wall. Re-measure once the flats are furnished.

Lantern hung under a floor needs the room parts to leave the lamp cells free: lamps are at flat 1 y12 and flat 2 y17 at x a+2, a+4, a+9 and z 11, 14, 18, 20, 22, plus lobby (x l0, z 9 and 20), aisle (a+4, 2, 23), loft (y19), and rear yard (doorX-1, 2, 26). Rooms should build around them.

Elements item 'Lit interiors via lanterns … no dark cells' is not fully ticked: it waits on the room measurement above. The lobby front lanterns (`lobby_door`) belong to frontage (part 4), not this part.
No candles: `candle` is not in palette.json, so the trade's shop-window candles were not used. Lanterns only.

waste.what: Re-measuring the light map by hand after each lamp change, and choosing lamp columns by reading the ASCII grid cell by cell.
waste.cost: 3 make+light cycles, about 6 min; the rest of the coordinates were worked out by hand from the plan's a-offsets.
waste.tool: An `mcd light --suggest` that proposes the minimal set of hung or standing lantern spots, each checked for air and a supporting block, to bring every floor cell to 8+ (the room command does this only for the shell, not for the whole building).

waste.what: Checking by hand whether each lamp cell is air and supported before calling g.set, because the grid's isAir and blockAt are not documented in the kit.
waste.cost: About 10 lines of helper code written from reading structure.mjs.
waste.tool: A documented `lamp(g, x, y, z, {hanging})` helper in vocab/ that does the support check and writes the lantern state, shared by all lighting parts.

waste.what: Looking for the rear-yard lamps in the back elevation tile, which does not show them at that scale.
waste.cost: One render plus a Read of the tile.
waste.tool: A `mcd render --view` on the yard, or a close-up tile listed for small features at the rear door.

companions.task: Build the partitions and furniture of the flats and lofts after the lamp cells are fixed, leaving the hung lantern cells and the standing lamp cells free so the lights are not walled in or blocked.
Check the stair-well openings at flat 1 and flat 2 so the hung lanterns at x a+9 and z 17 to 22 have a solid block above them where the well is open.

structured_output.summary:
parts/lights.mjs places 53 lanterns: standing lamps in each lobby (2), the service aisle and each rear door's yard; hung lamps under flat 1 and flat 2 ceilings and standing lamps in the lofts.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the lighting line reports 53 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check shows no lantern floating or unsupported.
Every lobby floor cell is at 8+; flats and lofts are dim-to-lit with 1–2 dark cells left per flat 2, measured on the empty shell before the room parts furnish it.
left: Flat 2 still has dark floor cells on the empty shell: 1 each in H1 and H2 and 2 in H3, at the rear corners and the H3 inner strip. Re-run `node $MCD light build.nbt --rooms rooms.json` after the room parts (furniture and partitions change the light) and add a lamp where a cell stays at 0.
Flat 1 cells sit at 4–5 (dim, not dark) on the shell: the stub rooms have not been built, so this is mostly wall. Re-measure once the flats are furnished.

Lantern hung under a floor needs the room parts to leave the lamp cells free: lamps are at flat 1 y12 and flat 2 y17 at x a+2, a+4, a+9 and z 11, 14, 18, 20, 22, plus lobby (x l0, z 9 and 20), aisle (a+4, 2, 23), loft (y19), and rear yard (doorX-1, 2, 26). Rooms should build around them.

Elements item 'Lit interiors via lanterns … no dark cells' is not fully ticked: it waits on the room measurement above. The lobby front lanterns (`lobby_door`) belong to frontage (part 4), not this part.
No candles: `candle` is not in palette.json, so the trade's shop-window candles were not used. Lanterns only.

waste.what: Re-measuring the light map by hand after each lamp change, and choosing lamp columns by reading the ASCII grid cell by cell.
waste.cost: 3 make+light cycles, about 6 min; the rest of the coordinates were worked out by hand from the plan's a-offsets.
waste.tool: An `mcd light --suggest` that proposes the minimal set of hung or standing lantern spots, each checked for air and a supporting block, to bring every floor cell to 8+ (the room command does this only for the shell, not for the whole building).

waste.what: Checking by hand whether each lamp cell is air and supported before calling g.set, because the grid's isAir and blockAt are not documented in the kit.
waste.cost: About 10 lines of helper code written from reading structure.mjs.
waste.tool: A documented `lamp(g, x, y, z, {hanging})` helper in vocab/ that does the support check and writes the lantern state, shared by all lighting parts.

waste.what: Looking for the rear-yard lamps in the back elevation tile, which does not show them at that scale.
waste.cost: One render plus a Read of the tile.
waste.tool: A `mcd render --view` on the yard, or a close-up tile listed for small features at the rear door.

companions.task: Build the partitions and furniture of the flats and lofts after the lamp cells are fixed, leaving the hung lantern cells and the standing lamp cells free so the lights are not walled in or blocked.
Check the stair-well openings at flat 1 and flat 2 so the hung lanterns at x a+9 and z 17 to 22 have a solid block above them where the well is open.
